description: Reconstructs Fu Hao’s military, familial and ritual authority in the late Shang court by comparing oracle-bone inscriptions with her intact tomb at Yinxu. Explains divination, bronze and jade production, ancestral offerings, sacrifice, archaeological identification and the limits of inferring a personal biography or general women’s status from elite records.

period.label: c. 1200 BCE · Fu Hao’s late Shang court
period.note: The narration explicitly places Fu Hao around the thirteenth century BCE, usually near 1200 BCE. The single approximate anchor is neither a birth/death date nor a dated campaign. The 1976 excavation is modern evidence, not the ancient setting.
